prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an indoor corner layout with no people present, featuring a television screen on a small round table directly in front of the camera wearer at roughly 1.0 to 1.5 metres away, a white game console and controller sitting in front of and slightly below the TV at about 0.8 to 1.2 metres, and a lit glass aquarium or terrarium to the left at roughly 1.5 to 2.0 metres (about 0.5 metres left of the TV). Across the five frames, the camera wearer pitches downward and turns slightly right while approaching the table, bringing the game console, table legs, and a roll of toilet paper on the floor below the table into arm's reach (under 0.8 metres) by frames 4 and 5 while the aquarium exits the left edge of the view and the top of the TV is cropped out. The Console and controller partially occlude the lower bezel of the TV in frames 1 to 4, and the tabletop occludes the floor items below it until the camera tilts down. Compared to the dark RGB frames, the depth map clearly reveals the continuous planar geometry of the right-hand wall, the curved table legs in frame 5, and the foreground separation between the console and the TV screen behind it. However, the depth map is unreliable in the dark upper and left regions of frames 1 to 3 where the ceiling and background walls are inconsistently estimated as either very near (bright) or infinitely far (black), and the glowing aquarium on the left is rendered nearly pitch black as if much farther away than its true ~1.5-metre distance.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map detects no people in the scene and isolates only two rectangular regions across frames 1 to 4: a green mask on the left at roughly 1.5 to 2.0 metres from the camera wearer and a light-blue mask in the centre-right at roughly 1.0 to 1.5 metres, spaced about 0.3 to 0.5 metres apart horizontally. In frames 1 to 3 both masks remain at a steady mid-range distance just beyond arm's reach, then shift upward in frame 4 as the camera tilts down, and disappear completely in frame 5 when the aquarium leaves the field of view and only the bottom corner of the right screen remains visible at the top-right edge. The bottom edge of the light-blue TV mask shows jagged cutouts where the foreground game console and white controller (roughly 0.8 to 1.2 metres away, reaching arm's reach in frames 4 and 5) partially occlude the lower screen border. While the map cleanly delineates the outer boundaries of the two illuminated rectangular structures against the dark room, it provides no information beyond what is already bright in the RGB image. Furthermore, the segmentation is unreliable because it misclassifies the lit glass aquarium/terrarium on the left as a 'tv', fails to detect the partially cropped TV in frame 5, and completely misses the foreground game console, controller, small table, and toilet paper roll on the floor.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all five frames, indicating that no human bodies, heads, or hands—neither other people nor the camera wearer's own limbs—are detected anywhere in the scene. Consequently, there are no people facing or looking toward the camera wearer, and the only objects within or entering arm's reach (under 0.8 metres in frames 4 and 5) are inanimate items visible in the RGB and depth views: the white game console, the controller on its left, the small table, and the toilet paper roll on the floor below. As the camera wearer turns slightly right and tilts downward from the mid-range TV (1.0 to 1.5 metres away) and left-side aquarium (1.5 to 2.0 metres away) toward the floor across the five frames, no body parts ever enter the field of view or become occluded by the furniture. This empty map confirms the absence of people even in the heavily shadowed regions of the room where the RGB image is nearly black, and it shows no false-positive skeleton detections despite the human-like video game character visible on the TV screen in frame 4.
